AC.name: Air Canada
steps: Select 'Flight Delay or Cancellation' from the dropdown menu.
Enter your 13-digit ticket number or 6-character booking reference.
Submit your banking details when prompted.

AF.name: Air France
steps: Log into your Flying Blue account, or continue as a guest.
Select 'Request Compensation' under the EU261 category.
Provide your flight details and await their email response.

BA.name: British Airways
steps: Scroll down to 'Claim compensation for a delayed or cancelled flight'.
Login with your Executive Club account to auto-fill your details, or proceed manually.

DL.name: Delta Air Lines
steps: Select 'File a Complaint' -> 'Flight Delay/Cancellation'.
Delta usually issues eCredits automatically, but you must demand a cash refund if you were Involuntarily Denied Boarding (Bumped).

LH.name: Lufthansa
steps: Navigate to 'Flight Disruptions' -> 'Compensation in the event of flight irregularities'.
Fill out the online EU261 form with your PNR (Booking Code).

EK.name: Emirates
steps: If you departed from an EU or UK airport, explicitly mention you are claiming under EU261/UK261.
Submit your ticket details and wait for their team to process the transfer.

UA.name: United Airlines
steps: If you were bumped (Involuntary Denied Boarding), specify that you are requesting your DOT-mandated cash compensation.

AA.name: American Airlines
steps: Choose 'Customer Relations' and select 'Flight Delay/Cancellation'.
If you were bumped from an overbooked flight, clearly state your demand for DOT compensation.

WS.name: WestJet
steps: Wait until exactly 72 hours have passed since your flight arrived (they reject early claims).
Enter your Reservation Code and submit your banking information.

TS.name: Air Transat
steps: Select 'Compensation Request' for APPR or EU261.
Fill out the electronic form with your booking reference.

FR.name: Ryanair
steps: Do NOT use a third-party agency, Ryanair strictly requires passengers to submit directly through this form.
Enter your booking reference and email address.

U2.name: easyJet
steps: Select your flight from your account history or enter your booking reference.
Submit your bank details for direct transfer.

W6.name: Wizz Air
steps: Log into your Wizz Air account.
Select the 'Flight Disruption' category and submit your EU261/UK261 claim.

TP.name: TAP Air Portugal
steps: Select 'Complaints' and then 'Flight Delays/Cancellations'.
Provide your booking reference and state your rights under EU261.

VY.name: Vueling
steps: Enter your Booking Code and Email.
Submit your bank details for EU261 compensation.

TK.name: Turkish Airlines
steps: Select 'New Feedback' and 'Flight Disruption'.
Quote the SHY-PASS or EU261 regulation depending on your departure airport.

PC.name: Pegasus Airlines
steps: Select 'Delay/Cancellation' as the topic.
Submit your PNR code to claim under Turkish SHY-PASS or EU261 regulations.

F9.name: Frontier Airlines
steps: File a formal complaint using their web form.
State you are requesting a refund for a controllable delay/cancellation under US DOT guidelines.

NK.name: Spirit Airlines
steps: Select 'Flight Disruption' as your issue.
Demand compensation per their DOT Customer Service Plan for controllable delays.

B6.name: JetBlue
steps: JetBlue automatically issues travel credit for controllable delays.
If you were bumped involuntarily, use the form to demand a cash refund.

WN.name: Southwest Airlines
steps: Select 'Complaint' -> 'Flight Delay or Cancellation'.
Southwest generally provides LUV Vouchers, but you must demand a cash refund if you choose not to travel.

F8.name: Flair Airlines
steps: Submit an APPR claim form via their Help Center.
Wait 30 days for a response before escalating to the CTA.

WG.name: Sunwing Airlines
steps: Use their dedicated APPR Delay Claim portal.
Provide your booking reference and bank details.

SK.name: SAS Scandinavian
steps: Use their dedicated EU261 claim form.
Submit your booking reference and wait for their response.

BY.name: TUI Airways
steps: Enter your TUI booking reference.
Submit your details for UK261/EU261 compensation.

EW.name: Eurowings
steps: Enter your booking code and name.
Follow the EU261 prompts to receive your compensation.

V7.name: Volotea
steps: Select 'Flight Disruption' in their contact form.
Quote your EU261 rights for compensation.

EI.name: Aer Lingus
steps: Select 'Flight Delay/Cancellation Compensation'.
Submit your PNR for EU261 processing.

KL.name: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines
steps: Log in to your Flying Blue account or use your booking code.
Request EU261 compensation directly through their portal.

IB.name: Iberia
steps: Select 'Claims' and then 'Flight Delays'.
Provide your booking reference for EU261 processing.

UX.name: Air Europa
steps: Navigate to the Claims section.
Submit your ticket details for EU261 compensation.

SQ.name: Singapore Airlines
steps: If departing from the EU/UK, explicitly state you are claiming under EU261/UK261.
Provide your e-ticket number.

QR.name: Qatar Airways
steps: Submit a feedback form.
If departing from the EU/UK, demand EU261/UK261 compensation.

LA.name: LATAM Airlines
steps: Submit a claim under Brazil's ANAC 400 or EU261 if departing Europe.

QF.name: Qantas
steps: Submit a customer care form.
Specify if your flight falls under EU261 or APPR jurisdictions.

AI.name: Air India
steps: Submit a grievance form.
Quote EU261 or UK261 if departing from those regions.

SU.name: Aeroflot
steps: Use the feedback form to submit a claim.
Quote the applicable jurisdiction.

NZ.name: Air New Zealand
steps: Submit your PNR and flight details.
Quote EU261 or APPR if departing from Europe or Canada.

JL.name: Japan Airlines
steps: Submit a customer feedback form.
Specify EU261 rights if departing from Europe.

NH.name: All Nippon Airways (ANA)
steps: Submit a query to customer support.
State your EU261 claim details if applicable.

CX.name: Cathay Pacific
steps: Use the email form to submit your claim.
Specify EU261 if departing Europe.
